subject: Los Angeles ‘mansion’ tax unsurprisingly backfires
posts:
Los Angeles's luxury 'mansion' tax was sold as a progressive fix for affordable housing, but UCLA studies reveal it crippled home construction.
Evidence: intended housing funds, 9000 lost units, builder pullbacks
#Aletheia #Housing #USPol

Proponents claimed taxing high-end property sales would easily fund public housing without harming overall real estate supply or economic growth.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

In reality, the mansion tax choked luxury development and reduced overall home-construction permits by thousands, driving builders into surrounding suburbs.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Top-down punitive taxation was marketed as altruistic aid, but predictable supply destruction hurt the very renters it aimed to help.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 11.2, Uncertainty z: 4)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Tax Policy Framing: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Masks supply destruction as equity.
- Economic Reality: FAIL (-0.9, -0.9) — 9,000 lost homes and fleeing builders.
Los Angeles enacted a transfer tax on high-value property sales to fund affordable housing, but researchers at UCLA found it triggered a severe chilling effect on new residential construction.

The Poison:
Punitive market interventions dressed up as compassion often destroy the exact resources they seek to redistribute, worsening housing scarcity.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing a moral wish (WHAT we want to fund) with a physical reality (HOW supply curves respond to predatory taxes).

Social Physics Analysis:
Politicians run a smart selfish maneuver by using a popular class grievance as a pretext to extract revenue, ignoring basic market physics and displacing the resulting shortage onto everyday buyers.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Punitive extraction creates structural scarcity under the guise of compassion.

The Unavoidable Truth: Punitive luxury taxes can severely depress overall housing supply and drive development out of the city.

The Unavoidable Lie: Slapping heavy fees on high-end sales magically generates public funds without any negative side effects.

Alethekanon:
Proponents traded economic reality for moral signaling, weaponizing envy while ignoring the predictable collapse of home construction.

Awwthekanon:
It breaks my heart seeing families priced out because well-meaning policies end up choking off the very homes people desperately need.

Brothekanon:
Classic government math: slap a huge tax on building houses, wonder why nobody wants to build houses anymore.

Spirithekanon:
"Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right." Proverbs 16:8 FAIL
Righteous rhetoric cannot mask the injustice of policies that generate scarcity and harm the vulnerable.
